theater: 遼東半島與山東威海衛

battle.name: 乙未戰爭
battle.theater: 遼東半島與山東威海衛
battle.brief: 光緒二十年夏，中日為朝鮮起兵，戰火由朝鮮東岸延燒至遼東半島，最後在山東威海衛收束。卡面的加特林機槍是當時最新的連發速射武器：日軍以十八式、二十式機槍配屬師團，清軍則靠進口機與金陵製造局仿製品守旅順、威海衛砲台，與野砲同列，卻始終補不上火力、指揮與後勤的落差。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 大清帝國與日本帝國為朝鮮的歸屬開戰，戰場橫跨朝鮮半島、黃海與遼東半島，山東威海衛是收尾的戰場。日本一方由明治政府於一八八五年設立的參謀本部統籌全局：陸軍以師團為基本作戰單位，混成第一師團由山縣有朋率領，負責攻擊平壤，第二師團由乃木希典率領，在牙山一線抵擋清軍，第五師團由溝瀨雄亮負責遼東方向，攻取旅順與威海衛的第二軍由陸軍元帥大山岩指揮；海軍方面，一八九四年成立的聯合艦隊以松島為旗艦，司令長官先後為坪井航三與伊東祐亨，黃海海戰正是這支艦隊在鴨綠江口外海與北洋艦隊的遭遇。清廷一方由北洋大臣李鴻章總攬軍務，調兵、籌餉、議和都經他手；北洋海軍以提督丁汝昌統率，旗艦定遠、鎭遠次之，北洋陸軍在朝鮮由葉志超、聶士成等分領各營。朝鮮王朝以高宗為主，名義上附庸於清廷，東學黨起義攻入漢城後，朝鮮王庭向清廷求援，清廷出兵，朝鮮內戰於是成了兩國交鋒的場合。英、美、俄、法、德等國在戰事中都守住中立與商利，沒有一國出兵干涉，直到戰後俄、法、德三國以共同施壓促成遼東半島歸還。
countriesEn: Qing China and the Empire of Japan went to war over the allegiance of Korea, and the battlefield ran across the Korean peninsula, the Yellow Sea and the Liaodong peninsula, with Weihaiwei in Shandong as the theatre in which the war was closed out. On the Japanese side the overall direction of the war lay with the General Staff, established by the Meiji government in 1885. The army fought in divisions: the Mixed First Division under Yamagata Aritomo was responsible for the attack on Pyongyang; the Second Division under Nogi Maresuke held the line at Asan against the Qing troops; the Fifth Division under Mizokoro Yuryo drove up the Liaodong coast; and the Second Army, commanded by the field marshal Oyama Iwao, took Port Arthur and Weihaiwei. At sea the Combined Fleet, constituted in 1894, flew its flag from the Matsushima, with Tsuboi Kozo and then Ito Sukeyuki as commander-in-chief, and it was this fleet that met the Beiyang Fleet off the mouth of the Yalu in the Battle of the Yellow Sea. On the Qing side the North Sea Minister Li Hongzhang held the war in his hands: troops were moved, money was raised and the peace was negotiated through him. The Beiyang Navy was commanded by the admiral Ding Ruchang, with the Dingyuan as flagship and the Zhenyuan next in precedence, and the Beiyang Army in Korea was distributed among the detachments under men such as Ye Zhichao and Nie Shicheng. Korea, ruled by King Gojong, was nominally a vassal of the Qing; when the Donghak Peasant rising took Seoul the Korean court asked Qing China for troops, and a rebellion was thus turned into a clash between the two states. Britain, the United States, Russia, France and Germany all sat out the war, guarding their commercial interests without a shot, and none of them intervened militarily; it was only after the war that Russia, France and Germany combined their pressure to bring about the return of the Liaodong peninsula.
people: 留下姓名的，多在兩端的核心。明治天皇睦仁自一八八〇年代起推動海外擴張，參謀本部長山縣有朋是整套作戰計劃的推手，也是攻擊平壤的指揮官。第二師團長乃木希典在牙山以孤軍頂住清軍與朝鮮義兵的猛攻，所部折損近半，幾至全滅，其後率部參與平壤與遼東戰役。陸軍元帥大山岩以第二軍司令官的身份督率攻取旅順與威海衛兩處要地。聯合艦隊司令長官坪井航三在黃海海戰中坐鎮旗艦松島，臨陣指揮全艦，松島被擊中十餘次而始終未沉。首相伊藤博文是唯一親赴前線的日本政治家，他主導對清交涉，最終在馬關與李鴻章對談成交。清廷一方，北洋大臣李鴻章主持全局，先後調兵、籌餉，最後代表清廷簽訂和約，返國後留任北洋大臣，並於翌年赴俄交涉。提督丁汝昌在威海衛陷落前夜服毒殉節，麾下劉步蟾、鄧世昌等人分頭力戰，鄧世昌在黃海海戰中率致遠艦冒死衝撞日艦吉野，艦沉人亡。旅順守將姜英、馬玉昆皆死於城破之日，葉志超自平壤潰退時丟棄大量輜重。袁世凱以駐朝鮮總理營務處的身分平定東學黨起義，事後在漢城主持朝鮮王室的改組交涉。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive are mostly at the two centres of the war. The Emperor Meiji, Mutsuhito, had been driving overseas expansion since the 1880s, and the chief of the General Staff, Yamagata Aritomo, was the man behind the whole operational plan and the commander of the attack on Pyongyang. Nogi Maresuke, commanding the Second Division, stood at Asan with a single division against the Qing army and the Korean irregulars, lost close to half of his men there, very nearly being wiped out, and afterwards led his troops in the fighting at Pyongyang and in Liaodong. The field marshal Oyama Iwao, commanding the Second Army, directed the taking of Port Arthur and Weihaiwei, the two key positions on which the war turned. The commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet, Tsuboi Kozo, sat on the flagship Matsushima during the Battle of the Yellow Sea and directed the fleet in person, the Matsushima being struck more than a dozen times without being sunk. Prime Minister Ito Hirobumi was the only Japanese politician to go near the front, and he led the negotiations with the Qing, and finally came to terms with Li Hongzhang at Shimonoseki. On the Qing side the North Sea Minister Li Hongzhang directed everything, moving troops, raising money and finally signing the peace on behalf of the court; he kept his post after returning, and travelled to Russia the following year. The admiral Ding Ruchang took poison on the eve of the fall of Weihaiwei rather than surrender, and under him Liu Buchan and Deng Shichang fought on in different parts of the line; at the Battle of the Yellow Sea Deng Shichang drove the Zhiyuan at the Japanese cruiser Yoshino in a desperate attempt to ram her, and the ship went down with her men. The defenders of Port Arthur, Jiang Ying and Ma Yukun, both died on the day the city fell, and Ye Zhichao abandoned a great quantity of baggage and stores as he fled from Pyongyang. Yuan Shikai, in charge of the Qing office for the conduct of military affairs in Korea, put down the Donghak rising and afterwards presided over the negotiations with the Korean court over the reform of the government.
kits: 卡面的加特林機槍出自一八六〇年前後的美國，是多管人力轉動的連發速射武器：槍管轉動一周完成六次發射，後坐力分散在六次擊發之間，因此能在短時間內傾瀉大量彈藥，是最早一代能壓制密集隊形的火器。這場戰爭的兩端都有它。日軍在一八九三年前後把十八式五連裝與二十式七連裝定為制式，由大阪與名古屋的兵工廠製造，配屬各師團的機關砲兵隊，在平壤攻門與遼東追擊中使用；清軍的加特林則一半靠進口，一半出自南京金陵製造局在一八八〇年代末的仿製品，另有一批由湖北槍炮廠承接，各營把它架在旅順、威海衛的砲台與城頭，與野砲、速射砲、弓弩並列，用來對付衝鋒中的人海。實際運用的弱點同樣清楚：加特林耗電，須以人力搖車或畜力發電機驅動，攜行需要數人與牲畜，彈藥消耗極快，而遼東與山東的補給線又被切斷。野砲方面，日本用二十八厘米與十五厘米野砲，射程、精度與射速都勝一籌；清軍仍以克虜式前膛炮為主，後膛炮比例有限。攻城器材方面，日軍以工兵配合坑道爆破攻破旅順城防，又以魚雷艇夜航入港、在威海衛海峽佈雷封鎖航道；水陸運輸主要靠軍馬、牛車與海運，而清軍從山東往遼東的輸送線長達數百公里，冬季氣候惡劣，人員物資的補充極慢。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun on the card came out of the United States around 1860. It is a multi-barrelled, hand-cranked repeating weapon: the barrels revolve once for every six discharges, the recoil is spread across those six shots, and the result is that a large quantity of ammunition can be poured out in a very short time, which made it the first generation of weapon capable of pinning down a massed formation. Both ends of this war had it. The Japanese army made the Type 18 five-barrel and the Type 20 seven-barrel Gatling its standard weapons in the years around 1893, manufacturing them at the Osaka and Nagoya arsenals and attaching them to the machine-gun companies of the divisions, where they were used against the gates of Pyongyang and in the pursuit in Liaodong. Half of the Qing Gatlings were imported and half were copies made at the Jinling Arsenal in Nanjing in the late 1880s, with a further batch turned out by the Hubei Arsenal. The batteries mounted them on the emplacements and walls of Port Arthur and Weihaiwei, ranged alongside field guns, quick-firing guns and crossbows, and used them against the massed foot that came at them. The weaknesses of the weapon in service are just as clear: the Gatling consumed electricity, had to be driven by a hand crank or a horse-drawn generator, needed several men and animals to move, and burned ammunition at a furious rate, while the supply lines into Liaodong and Shandong were cut. In the artillery arm Japan was markedly superior, with 28-centimetre and 15-centimetre field guns of better range, accuracy and rate of fire, while the Qing army still relied on Krupp-pattern muzzle-loading pieces with only a limited proportion of breech-loaders. For siege work the Japanese used sappers and mine galleries to reduce the defences of Port Arthur, and torpedo boats that ran in by night to lay mines across the approaches to Weihaiwei. Movement of men and matériel depended on pack horses, ox carts and coastal shipping, while the Qing line of communication from Shandong into Liaodong ran for several hundred kilometres through a severe winter, and resupply was painfully slow.
tactics: 日軍的打法，是把整場戰爭拆成幾段可以速決的攻勢，再逐一殲滅。朝鮮方向，先以艦隊在豐島外海攻擊清軍運輸船隻，切斷鴨綠江與平壤之間的水路，再由第二師團在牙山正面抵擋、第一師團迂迴到清軍側後，逼使清軍放棄平壤。遼東方向，第五師團沿海岸推進，依次奪取蓋平、大連，再由工兵配合二十八厘米砲連續轟擊旅順要塞，最終以坑道爆破攻破城防。威海衛一役則是海陸並行：艦隊以魚雷艇夜航入港，擊沉或擊傷泊於港內的北洋軍艦，日軍同時在威海衛灣北岸與劉公島一線強行登陸，砲兵逐座壓制海岸砲台。攻堅之中，日軍步兵習慣以大隊縱隊推進，接近到一二百米內再以刺刀衝鋒，掩體多用簡單胸牆與散兵坑。清軍則完全相反，倚重環形砲壘與城牆死守，卻缺乏統一指揮，通訊多靠傳令兵與書信。平壤之戰，清軍在城北各門外修築堡壘，試圖以交叉火力封住進攻道路，日軍集中野砲逐個壓制堡壘，再由工兵爆破城門；城門被突破之後，清軍的整條防線隨即崩潰，全軍退回鴨綠江一線。旅順與威海衛的守軍同樣把希望寄托在砲台與永備工事上，但海路被封、陸路援兵斷絕之後，砲台再堅固也只能孤立待援。
tacticsEn: The Japanese method was to break the whole war into engagements that could be decided quickly, and then to destroy the Qing army in detail. In Korea the fleet first struck at Chinese transports off Pungdo, cutting the water route between the Yalu and Pyongyang; the Second Division was then made to stand at Asan while the First Division swung round behind the Qing position and forced the evacuation of Pyongyang. In Liaodong the Fifth Division pushed up the coast, taking Gaiping and then Dalian, and the sappers worked with the 28-centimetre guns to batter the defences of Port Arthur over four weeks, the galleries being finally blown and the position collapsing. The Weihaiwei operation was naval and amphibious at once: torpedo boats came in by night to sink or damage the Beiyang ships lying in the harbour, while the army forced a landing on the northern shore of Weihaiwei Bay and on the island of Liugongdao, its artillery working over the coastal batteries one at a time. In the assaults the Japanese infantry habitually advanced in battalion columns, closed to within a hundred or two hundred metres and then went in with the bayonet, and their cover was little more than breastworks and shallow pits. The Qing fought exactly the reverse way, depending on ring fortresses and city walls to hold out, but without unified command and with orders carried by runners and letters. At Pyongyang the Qing had built redoubts outside the northern gates in the hope of crossing their fire over the approaches; the Japanese brought up massed field guns, beat down the redoubts in turn, and blew the gates with sappers, and once the gate was breached the whole line collapsed and the army fell back to the Yalu. The garrisons of Port Arthur and Weihaiwei put the same trust in their batteries and permanent works, but once the sea route was sealed and the land route to their relief cut, the batteries, however strong, could only wait in isolation.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。戰爭自一八九四年七月二十五日豐島海戰起，至一八九五年四月十七日簽訂馬關條約止，前後約八個月又二十三天；台灣方向的戰事延續到該年秋冬。平壤之戰，日軍投入的混成第一師團兵力約一萬六千至一萬七千人，清軍約一萬二千至一萬五千人，日軍付出約二百人的陣亡代價，清軍的陣亡與被俘以數千計。牙山一戰，日軍第二師團一部約五千人，對上清軍四路大軍與朝鮮義兵，該部幾乎全滅，傷亡近二千人。旅順守軍約四千人，陷落時折損殆盡；威海衛守軍約五千人，北洋艦隊十餘艘或沉或降，艦隊官兵死傷以數千計。黃海海戰，致遠艦一艦沉沒，艦上官兵大部殉難；日方只折十餘人陣亡、數十人負傷，旗艦松島被擊中十餘次。條約賠款白銀二億兩，分十年支付；割讓遼東半島、台灣全島及所有附屬島嶼、澎湖列島；另開沙市、重慶、蘇州、杭州四處為商埠。加特林各型略有差異，早期六管型每分鐘約百發，一八七〇年代以後的改進型可達三四百發，射程八百至一千二百米，操作需二至四人並另備電源，野戰時的實際有效射擊距離多在五百米上下。日軍二十八厘米砲的射程明顯超過清軍所用諸砲，這是旅順攻堅得以奏效的技術前提。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war began with the engagement off Pungdo on 25 July 1894 and ended with the signature of the Treaty of Shimonoseki on 17 April 1895, about eight months and twenty-three days in all, with the fighting in Taiwan running on into the autumn of that year. At Pyongyang the Japanese committed the Mixed First Division, some sixteen to seventeen thousand men, against twelve to fifteen thousand Qing troops, and paid about two hundred dead for it, while Qing dead and captured ran into the thousands. At Asan a detachment of about five thousand from the Second Division faced four Qing columns reinforced with Korean irregulars, and was very nearly wiped out, with close to two thousand casualties. The Port Arthur garrison numbered about four thousand and was virtually destroyed when the place fell; the Weihaiwei garrison was around five thousand, and more than a dozen Beiyang ships were sunk or surrendered, with naval casualties running into the thousands. In the Battle of the Yellow Sea the Zhiyuan went down with the great majority of her crew, while the Japanese lost only a dozen or so dead and several dozen wounded, the flagship Matsushima being struck more than a dozen times. The treaty provided for an indemnity of 200 million taels of silver payable over ten years, the cession of the Liaodong peninsula, the whole island of Taiwan with all its dependencies and the Pescadores, and the opening of Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou as treaty ports. The Gatling itself varied by type: the early six-barrel models fired about a hundred rounds a minute, and the improved types of the 1870s reached three or four hundred; the range was from eight hundred to twelve hundred metres, two to four men were needed to work the gun and a separate source of power had to be carried, and in the field the effective shooting distance was nearer five hundred metres. The range of the Japanese 28-centimetre gun was plainly superior to that of the pieces the Qing used, and that was the technical precondition for the success of the siege of Port Arthur.
cause: 打起來的緣由，最外面是朝鮮。朝鮮王朝名義上附庸於清廷，實際上被日本視為第一步棋。一八八二年壬午兵變、一八八四年甲申政變之後，中日在朝鮮的角力日益加深；一八八五年伊藤博文與李鴻章在天津訂立關於朝鮮的條約，規定共同改革朝鮮，卻為日後的介入埋下伏筆。一八九四年初，朝鮮東學黨領導的農民起義攻入漢城，朝鮮王庭向清廷求援，清廷派兵入朝，日本隨即以朝鮮政府的名義邀請本國出兵，兩國兵馬在鴨綠江與漢城之間對峙，最終一八九四年七月二十五日日軍在豐島海面攻擊清軍運輸船，把一場平定內亂的軍事行動變成了開戰。往裡一層是日本的國策：明治政府自維新以來以富國強兵為目標，眼看西方列強在亞洲的據點已大半被瓜分，日本要在列強尚未趕到遠東之前搶先取得位置；而當時的國際環境也對日本有利，列強正忙於歐洲與美洲的糾葛，無暇插手遠東。最深的一層是清廷自身的失誤：北洋艦隊自一八八八年之後多年未添新艦，財政與官制改革半途而廢，朝鮮與遼東的情報與動員都顯得遲鈍，戰前既未決心也未準備，最後在戰場上才發覺自己已無法逆勢而動。
causeEn: Several layers of reason lie behind the fighting. The outermost was Korea. The Korean court was nominally a vassal of the Qing, but Japan treated it as the first piece on the board. After the Imo Mutiny of 1882 and the Gapsin Coup of 1884, the Sino-Japanese struggle over Korea deepened year by year; in 1885 Ito Hirobumi and Li Hongzhang concluded their agreement on Korea at Tientsin, providing for a joint reform of the peninsula, and that clause became the seed of later intervention. In the beginning of 1894 the peasant rising led by the Donghak sect took Seoul, the Korean court appealed to the Qing for troops, and the Qing sent them in. Japan then invited its own troops to Korea in the name of the Korean government, the two powers' forces closed on each other between the Yalu and Seoul, and on 25 July 1894 the Japanese struck at Chinese transports off Pungdo, turning what had been a peacekeeping operation into the opening of a war. One layer deeper lay Japanese national policy. The Meiji government had pursued the enrichment of the state and the strengthening of the army since the Restoration, and when it saw that most of the Western footholds in Asia had already been taken it meant to seize a position in the Far East before the Europeans arrived; the international moment suited Japan, for the powers were absorbed in their own quarrels in Europe and the Americas and had no appetite for an Asian war. At the deepest level was the Qing court's own failure. The Beiyang Fleet had taken on no new ships after 1888, fiscal and administrative reform had stalled halfway, and intelligence and mobilisation in Korea and Liaodong were slow; nothing had been decided and nothing prepared before the war, and only on the battlefield did the court discover that it could no longer shape events.
impact: 這場戰爭之後，清廷的處境從財政困難變成體系崩壞。賠款二億兩銀加上戰費，重壓之下不得不向列強借款，稅負隨之轉嫁；北洋海軍全軍覆沒，二十年間造起來的近代海軍一朝散盡，江南製造局、湖北槍炮廠的造艦與造槍規模隨之壓縮，但重建的呼聲自此不絕，張之洞在武昌、張佩綸在福州各自籌辦新式海軍。鄧世昌、丁汝昌的死，讓海軍二字第一次成為朝野共同語。國際層面上，中國被視為可以瓜分，戰後數年內德國取膠州、俄國取旅順、法國取廣州、英國取威海衛、美國取得菲律賓的呼聲此起彼伏，美國一八九九年的門戶開放宣言則是對這場瓜分熱潮的回應。維新思想亦在此際成形，康有為、梁啟超於一八九五年公車上書，請求變法，甲午的敗績由是成了變法的理由與動力。台灣與澎湖割讓之後，島上另組臺灣民主國以抗日，乙未年內仍有成建制的義軍與日軍對抗，直至翌年才告段落。朝鮮在實質上落入日本控制，日本得以在朝鮮推行改革並維持常駐軍，長期與俄國在東亞的角力就此鋪開。日本則以這場勝利為起點，確立了向大陸推進的路線，一八九六年度的擴軍計劃把軍費推上高峰，此後二十年間連續對外用兵，包括日俄戰爭。
impactEn: After this war the Qing court's predicament changed from financial difficulty to a breakdown of the whole structure. The indemnity of 200 million taels of silver, added to the cost of the campaign, obliged the government to borrow from the powers and the burden of tax fell on the people; the Beiyang Navy was destroyed root and branch and the modern fleet built up over twenty years vanished in a single stroke, the output of the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Hubei Arsenal being cut back, though the call for a new navy never stopped, with Zhang Zhidong at Wuchang and Zhang Peilun at Fuzhou each raising one. The deaths of Deng Shichang and Ding Ruchang made the navy for the first time a common word in court and country. Internationally China was now seen as open to partition, and within a few years Germany took Kiaochow, Russia took Port Arthur, France took the area around Guangzhou, Britain took Weihaiwei and the United States took the Philippines, while the Open Door declaration of 1899 was the American answer to that scramble. The reformist current also took shape in this period: Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao submitted the Gongche Shangshu in 1895 asking for changes in government, and the defeat of the war became both the argument for and the driving force behind the reform movement. After Taiwan and the Pescadores were ceded, the islanders formed the Republic of Formosa to resist, and organised bodies of irregulars fought the Japanese there through the year, until the resistance died out in the spring following. Korea in substance fell under Japanese control, Japan was able to impose its reforms on the peninsula and keep troops there, and the long rivalry with Russia in East Asia was thereby set in motion. For Japan the victory was the starting point of a continental policy: the expansion plan of 1896 pushed military spending to a new peak, and the twenty years that followed brought a run of wars abroad, beginning with the Russo-Japanese War.
result: 結果是中國戰敗，和約在李鴻章與伊藤博文之間簽訂。一八九五年四月十七日，馬關條約割讓遼東半島、台灣與澎湖，賠款白銀二億兩，開沙市、重慶、蘇州、杭州為商埠，並准日本在商埠設廠，同年六月換約。戰後數月，遼東半島的消息傳出，俄國、法國、德國以共同交涉的名義向日本施壓，要求歸還，一八九五年十一月日本接受，翌年商定界址，一八九八年三月正式交付，這是近代中國第一次以自己的交涉之力收回失地，卻也是列強在遠東聯手行動的開端。台灣方向，乙未戰爭在條約簽訂後仍在島上延續，日軍於同年三月底登陸，六月攻入臺南、月底取得澎湖，島上以唐景崧、丘逢甲為首的義軍抵抗到下半年才逐漸平息。主戰與主和的朝堂之爭也在此時落幕，翁同龢等主戰派被逐出朝廷，李鴻章以簽約之功留任北洋大臣，隨即赴俄遊歷並於翌年簽訂中俄密約。戰爭本身的勝負在威海衛就已定下，日本陸軍控制遼東與山東要點、海軍壓制黃海與渤海，剩下的只是條款怎麼寫、割地怎麼分的問題。
resultEn: The result was a Chinese defeat, and the peace was signed between Li Hongzhang and Ito Hirobumi. On 17 April 1895 the Treaty of Shimonoseki ceded the Liaodong peninsula, Taiwan and the Pescadores, imposed an indemnity of 200 million taels of silver, opened Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou as treaty ports and permitted Japanese factories there, and the ratifications were exchanged in June of the same year. Within months of the war's end the news of the cession brought Russia, France and Germany to press Japan jointly for its return; Japan accepted in November 1895, the boundary was negotiated the following year, and the territory was handed over in March 1898. That was the first time in modern history that China recovered lost territory by its own diplomacy, and equally the opening of joint action by the powers in the Far East. The fighting in Taiwan went on after the treaty: the Japanese landed at the end of March 1895, took Tainan in June and the Pescadores at the end of that month, and the island's irregular forces under men such as Tang Jingsong and Qiu Fengjia were only gradually worn down in the second half of the year. The court quarrel between the war party and the peace party ended at the same time: Weng Tonghe and the others who had urged a hard war were pushed out of office, Li Hongzhang was kept as North Sea Minister on the strength of having signed the treaty, and he travelled to Russia in the following year to conclude a secret agreement with that power. The military verdict of the war had already been settled at Weihaiwei, with the Japanese army holding the key points of Liaodong and Shandong and their navy dominating the Yellow Sea and the Bohai Gulf; what remained to be settled was only how the clauses should read and how the territory should be divided.
